text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm updating the internal comms template library after the last outage. want to make sure status page + external notifications + internal incident posts are aligned. suggestions welcome. :wave:

sanjay: thanks maya. can we standardize the sections first? e.g., Summary / Impact / Scope / Current Mitigation / Customer Action / ETA / Contact. short and scannable.

liam: agree. also add a clear line for 'user-facing risk' vs 'internal root cause work' so support/customer success know what to copy to customers.

emily: +1 to separate tones. proposed rules: external = plain english, no technical jargon, empathetic but not overpromising. internal = concise, include logs/metrics, next steps, who owns follow-up.

incident-bot: New incident template draft created by @maya. Use `/incident templates list` to view. Reaction: :white_check_mark:

maya: draft below. please poke holes. I'm trying to keep external messages <3 sentences where possible. internal posts can be longer.

maya: EXTERNAL STATUS PAGE TEMPLATE (short):
```
[Status] Investigating — [service name]
Summary: We are investigating an issue affecting [short description of feature].
Impact: Customers may experience [symptom]. Not all customers are affected.
What we're doing: Engineers are actively investigating and working on a mitigation.
Next update: by [ETA in minutes/hours] or sooner.
Contact: [link to support / status page / email]
```

maya: EXTERNAL CUSTOMER EMAIL / DM (friendly):
```
Hi [Customer name],
We're investigating an issue impacting [feature]. You may see [symptom]. Our engineers are working on a fix now. We'll send another update by [ETA]. We're sorry for the trouble — thanks for your patience.
Best,
The Redwood Inference Team
```

liam: nit: add optional severity tag for external like (Partial Degradation / Major Outage). also maybe add 'workaround' line if available.

maya: good call. update: added severity + workaround placeholder.

maya: INTERNAL INCIDENT SLACK POST (for channel #incidents or #eng-oncall):
```
INCIDENT [INC-YYYY-MM-DD-#] — [service] — [severity]
Summary: [1-2 sentence technical summary]
Impact: [what's failing, error rates, affected regions/customers]
Timeline: [timestamps of detection, mitigation started]
Current status: [Investigating / Mitigating / Identified / Resolved]
Mitigation in progress: [short bullets of actions taken e.g., rollback, toggle feature flag, scale up pool]
Owner(s): [oncall / eng lead / SRE]
Customer impact: [list customers or 'broad' / 'no data loss' etc.]
Next steps: [who will do what and ETA]
How to update status page: `/incident update-status [incident-id] "[State] — [short note]"`
Escalation: [oncall pager, pager escalation flow link]
Postmortem owner: [name] (assign later)
```

emily: recommend a short 'public-safe summary' line that support can paste unchanged into emails/Slack w/out internal details. keeps messaging consistent.

maya: yes — add `Customer-ready snippet:` section to internal post with 1-2 sentences sanitized for customer use.

sanjay: also call out legal/privacy check when incident involves customer data. template: `If PII/Customer Data exposure suspected, pause external messaging and tag @legal immediately.`

maya: added. also adding examples of phrasing to avoid (blame, root-cause speculation):
- DO NOT say: "we deployed a buggy change that caused X" in external messages.
- DO say: "we identified an issue and are working on a fix" and follow up with findings in postmortem.

liam: can we add short handoff snippet for on-call -> next shift? helps during long incidents. e.g.:
```
Handoff at [time UTC] from [oncall A] to [oncall B]:
- Current status: [Investigating / Mitigating]
- Key actions in last hour: [bullets]
- Open blockers: [bullets]
- Suggested next steps: [bullets]
- Contact: [pager link / slack dm]
```

maya: perfect. will include as `Handoff template` in the library.

incident-bot: Paging history for incident INC-2026-042: 03:07 oncall PAGER -> acknowledged by @sanjay at 03:09. Reaction: :rotating_light:

emily: policy note — for high-severity incidents, we should post a first external update within 15 minutes even if only to acknowledge. template should include that SLA.

maya: ok added line: `External acknowledgement SLA: 15 minutes for Sev1/Sev2`

sanjay: wording library should include a set of interchangeable placeholders to reduce cognitive load: [service], [symptom], [region], [customers_affected], [workaround], [eta], [incident_id]. ops-bot can auto-fill when incident is created.

maya: ops-bot integration: example command to create external status with placeholders:
```
/incident create --service inference-api --severity PartialDegradation --summary "Investigating increased error rates" --eta 30m --public-snippet "We're investigating increased errors affecting model responses."
```

liam: include a mini-checklist before sending external comms: 1) Confirm impact 2) Confirm PII/no-PII 3) Confirm next update ETA 4) Legal review if needed 5) Copy of public snippet in internal post.

maya: adding a short 'tone guide' half page:
- External: short, clear, avoid jargon, show empathy, give ETA/next update, don't speculate on cause.
- Internal: be factual, include metrics/logs, use timestamps, name owners, list next steps.

emily: I can help copyedit the templates for tone. i'll keep external messages under 2 sentences where feasible.

maya: thanks. final ask: can someone volunteer to test the ops-bot autofill with these placeholders in a staging incident tomorrow morning? I'll merge into the template library once tested.

liam: i'll take it. will run a dry-run at 09:30 UTC.

sanjay: +1. also would like a short training doc for support on how to copy/paste customer-ready snippets into Zendesk or directly into customer emails.

maya: adding follow-ups: @liam run bot test, @emily copyedit, @sanjay write support how-to. i'll post PR for the library after tests. thanks all! :heart:
